summary.intent: Win the Lio 'Keep the Line Running' hackathon challenge by analysing Soony's launch data, then building a general, adaptable agent product (poller, extraction, recompute, act with approvals) with a Today view for the senior buyer and a Launch view for procurement, plus demo and hand-in material.
summary.outcome: Found that the Collector's Edition (art books, failed statues) and later Standard (game cards, container) miss Sunday 20:00 despite the plan saying ok. Built and deployed a live app with versioned polling, supplier email actions, a phone approval loop, role views and a dry-run demo instance. Wrote README and demo script; UI polish ongoing, with the final hand-in at 12:00 still pending.

repo: Confidential Soony data lives in gitignored data/ (raw, drops, notes, img); .env holds SOONY_PORTAL_TOKEN and is gitignored while .env.example is committed.

The portal API has only GET /api/v1/files, /files/{path} and /archive.zip; there are no webhooks, so changes must be detected by polling the file list and comparing SHA-256. Files can be replaced under the same name, and formats can change.
Team workflow is in CLAUDE.md and PROGRESS.md; work is on branch jonas/today-flow. Entire records checkpoints only when repo files change and pushes them along with git push.

scripts/demo.sh (reset, snapshot, stop, CALLS=twilio) runs a demo instance at ask-soony-demo.stenglein.dev with all cases open, dry-run supplier emails (data/demo/state/dry_outbox.json), mailbox sync and portal polling off, and calls off.
Phone calls are controlled by ASK_CALL_PROVIDER (dry_run by default, Twilio costs about $0.38/min). ASK_SIGNOFF_SIMULATE=<seconds> auto-approves a passed-on case as a simulated Maren, off by default.
The frontend polls state every 5s (POLL_MS = 5000) and routines every 15s; it is not server push.

Sign-off flow: signoff.py, OkPage.tsx and /ok/<token> give a one-time passwordless approve/decline page; basic_auth.py lets valid links through; push goes to every subscribed device, with no per-person routing.
The shared mailbox sync used to write back a stale copy of the action log and lose records; fixed by appending under the shared lock (dd71984).
Backend server changes need a restart (live port 8000 and demo), while web/dist rebuilds are served fresh.

Data traps found: art book receipt overbooked 80,000 vs 8,000 (scan shows handwritten correction), 5,600 statues failed AQL but booked unrestricted, lid magnets are fitted by PackRight so the BOM line is a false alarm, sleeve rev B vs C conflict, Boise insists on EXW rather than DDP.
workflow: Run long analysis as a subagent (e.g. cross-checking 200 order confirmations and 59 scans) and write findings to a gitignored local notes file.
Verify UI fixes in a headless browser on the demo instance (e.g. pressing J ten times and counting highlighted rows) before committing.
Keep a separate demo instance with dry-run email so rehearsals never contact real suppliers.
Confirm with the user before actions with cost or external effects (Twilio calls, real emails, DNS changes); the first DNS record landed on the wrong tunnel and was corrected.
Do not commit confidential data, and keep sensitive values like portal passwords out of shared docs.

friction: Portal token was initially empty, which blocked the data pull (401) until the user supplied it.
Cloudflare Error 1033 on the demo hostname appeared because the DNS record first pointed at the wrong tunnel.
The mailbox-sync race silently dropped the 07:58 approval record, and the record had to be restored from the Sent folder.
Escalations ('pass it on') initially went nowhere, so Maren could not respond; stale prepared steps and duplicate routine steps created confusing UI.
J/K navigation disagreed with folded look-alike groups, causing the highlight to vanish and the order to jump.

Several UI wording and consistency issues: vague 'Standard is waiting for parts' sentence, Launch implying the user had to decide a case held by Maren, a routine showing 'Watching' while off, only 'show' clickable on a handled-cases line.
Data drops arrive unannounced (five files within 37 minutes), so the picture kept shifting; Safari caches old favicons.
open_items: Hand-in at 12:00: demo video, pitch deck and final rehearsal of the demo script end to end on the demo instance.
Several commits are not pushed (demo script, favicon, J/K, options count, key badges, ⌘↵ shortcuts, routine line fix).

Build the 'What still saves it' section on Launch (latest arrival per blocker, about 900 Collector's copies per hour of delay) and add the Felix question about getting container NHSU4471921 from the terminal to the DC.
Replay real supplier replies on the demo instance, and fold the repeated count questions into one case.
Top bar for the Maren role still says 'nothing needs you' because it counts Felix's list.
Delete the duplicate 'Ask Hamburg to count book stock' routine on live; decide on sending internal messages and escalations via push or Teams.
Push is not per-person, so a second device must play Maren; per-person routing is deferred; Teams webhook is not set up.
Decide whether to switch on real phone calls for the demo (notifications only) with CALLS=twilio.
Share the Claude doc and briefing page with the team only, delete the earlier doc if redundant, and change the portal password that appeared in Discord after the hack.
Open questions for the Lio engineers: whether portal data is identical across teams and whether supplier replies create portal files; Codex hooks still need approval in /hooks.
